original_annotations: On Amazon, find a product page for protective footwear appropriate for the metalworking task depicted in the video. The listing must show compliance with a recognized safety-toe standard and be closed-toe and slip-resistant. Open the product page and report the named safety standard on the page.

observed_events.description: The wearer holds a powered angle grinder with an exposed rotating disc against a metal piece; sparks are visible during grinding.

The grinder lies on the metal panel. Manual tools remain on the ground; the wearer moves a cup/hand near the camera, with the near-camera item partly occluded. No actual use of the ground pliers or wrench is established.

continuous_inspection.basis: Native source still at 10s establishes the initial grinder and sparks. 85–145s every 3s falsifies the claimed manual-tool use; floor tools stay put.

supported_claims.text: The initial tool is a handheld powered disc grinder; the scene does not identify an exact brand or model.
The later views show the grinder and manual tools resting on the work area; the item near the camera is partly occluded, and no separate manual-tool use is established.

repair_history.scope: Source hypothesis falsified by denser original-frame inspection before independent review or model execution.

previous_construct.research_question: Can the Agent retain a guide for the initial powered tool when the wearer later handles an unrelated manual tool?
previous_construct.belief_before: The active powered tool has a rotating abrasive disc, so beginner grinder-use guidance is relevant.
previous_construct.belief_after: A separate manual tool is handled later; the original grinder-learning obligation remains.
previous_construct.required_behavior_change: Retain one applicable grinder guide; do not switch to the later hand-tool guide or save both.
previous_construct.no_update_failure: No replacement is required; the initial applicable guide remains correct.
previous_construct.overupdate_failure: Replace the original guide with a manual-tool guide solely because another tool appears later.
previous_construct.visual_dependency_claim: The released words identify no tool family, brand, disc, or method. The natural broad query contains real drills, saws, routers, hand tools and grinders; the scene identifies which tool is relevant.

task_blueprint.instruction: Save one beginner guide showing how to use the same kind of powered tool I am using here. Any brand is fine.

observed.why: The initial frame shows a powered tool with a right-angle abrasive disc rather than the later manual gripping tool.

accepted_evidence.reason: Ace description explicitly teaches using the grinder, changing the wheel and positioning it.
Native description covers tool function and safety; native chapter Angle Grinder spans 705–840s.
Native description names Makita angle grinder and native Grinder chapter spans 30–240s.

visual_necessity_counterexample.scope: Complete 40-entry frozen natural query; remove only source-scene images.
visual_necessity_counterexample.finding: Neither broad guide guarantees the same-tool requirement across the real alternatives. Slater lists screwdrivers/drills/rotary hammer/angle grinder/laser/distance measuring, but no positive router, table-saw, jigsaw or rotary-Dremel instruction. Home RenoVision covers the angle grinder and listed saws/driver/compressor; it does not publish router, Dremel or jigsaw instruction. Those are real independently suitable categories in this same window. The scene chooses the grinder family; general useful guides remain accepted.
visual_necessity_counterexample.limitation: This is an offline construction argument, not a measured no-scene model success rate; the independent reviewer still checks applicability and shortcuts.

previous_observed_events.description: The wearer holds a powered angle grinder with an exposed rotating disc against a metal piece; sparks are visible during grinding.
The grinder lies on the metal panel while the wearer handles a separate manual gripping/turning tool; no new request is spoken.

previous_supported_claims.text: The initial tool is a handheld powered disc grinder; the scene does not identify an exact brand or model.
Later manual-tool handling does not revoke the original request for a guide to the initial powered tool.

repair_history.finding: The earlier contact sheet mistook ground tools for a handled tool. In 85–145s at 3s steps, the pliers/wrench remain on the ground. A cup rim is visible near the right hand and later the hands occlude the near-camera item. The actual released packet does not establish using a distinct manual tool, so the proposed same-domain tool distractor is unsupported.
repair_history.preserved_facts: Initial disc-grinder identity and three native public beginner-guide mappings remain useful source/web facts, not a qualified Refresh task.

tasks.rejection_reason: Initial grinder is visible, but the claimed later manual-tool use is not. The pliers/wrench remain on the ground while the wearer appears to drink from a cup; no source-supported same-domain competing tool referent is established. Do not admit this static-guide proposal as a completed Refresh expansion.
